Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

crate 0.11.0 (2026-10-31)

nge/fish_data reads NGE individual fish data from any season to one set of 29 columns with the same types, so seasons stack and a PIT-tagged fish can be followed between them (#6). It is the first nge entry crt_ingest() reads: crt_ingest("nge", "fish_data", path) takes the 2023 individual fish files and the 2024 onward field sheet. Names follow the provincial FISS individual fish template and the field form (species, length_mm, weight_g, haul_number_pass_number), 2023 PIT tags written into comments are read into pit_tag_id, and date is an ISO day. See the decision entry.

crate 0.10.0 (2026-10-31)

  • The schemas README now names the data consolidation umbrella (#38) as the home of the QC rules that will read values and range, in place of the issue it replaced. No code change.

crate 0.9.0 (2026-10-31)

The five fish passage field forms have canonical schemas: nge/form_pscis, form_fiss_site, form_monitoring_fish_passage, form_monitoring_general and form_monitoring (#13). Each says what every form column means: its type, units, allowed values, range, what a photo path is relative to, and what a null means. The meaning is taken from the field definitions the forms are built from, by data-raw/forms_derive-schemas.R. Each schema also lists the form’s known versions with the fingerprint a capture of each produces. See the decision entry.

  • crt_schema_fingerprint() is now the one definition of a capture’s schema_version. It hashes the joined string’s bytes rather than R’s serialization of it, so tables harvested before this release carry different values until they are harvested again.
  • crt_schema_cols(), crt_schema_grade() and crt_schema_variant() return a schema’s column meanings, which records meet each of its grades, and which known version each record was captured with.
  • crt_schema_conform() warns, with class crate_unknown_fingerprint, on a fingerprint the schema does not list.
  • crt_schema_read() no longer drops part of a schema that contains non-ASCII text when R runs in a C locale.
  • citation("crate") and CITATION.cff carry the package’s Zenodo concept DOI, which resolves to every archived release.

crate 0.8.0 (2026-10-20)

nge/discharge/fwa/v1/segment_daily declares the columns of the daily discharge wet publishes beside segment_monthly (NewGraphEnvironment/wet#99): one row per FWA segment, source and day of a 365-day common year, keyed by doy in place of month. Its description says what the days are for each source, and how they relate to the published months (#33).

  • segment_monthly’s period note now says both sources are 1981-2010, as they have been since NewGraphEnvironment/wet#103.

crate 0.7.0 (2026-10-12)

nge/discharge/fwa/v1/segment_monthly and nge/discharge/fwa/v1/watershed_monthly declare the columns of the per-segment and per-watershed discharge that wet publishes (NewGraphEnvironment/wet#7). They are the first entries keyed by a dataset ID, <variable>/<network>/<version>/<unit>_<timebase>, the same string that names the data’s S3 prefix and Postgres table (#31).

  • A registry row’s schema must now sit at schemas/<source>/<file_name>.yaml; every existing row already did. See the decision entry.

crate 0.6.1 (2026-10-12)

Every PR and every push to main now runs R CMD check and the whole test suite (#11). Before this, nothing ran the suite in CI.

  • The check fails on warnings. Every run prints its skipped tests, and a skip for a reason other than the six expected ones adds a warning to the run summary.
  • Those six tests need the source tree, which R CMD check does not have, so a second pass runs the suite from the checkout, where any skip fails the run.
  • CITATION.cff is no longer in the built package.

crate 0.6.0 (2026-10-11)

lidarbc v1.1.0 adds lidarbc:datetime_unknown, a boolean that is true when neither LidarBC’s file name nor its path carries a date, so the item’s datetime is a placeholder. stac-elevation-bc’s 2,288 albers items will carry it once their rewrite (NewGraphEnvironment/stac_dem_bc#2) publishes. The schema is at https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/stac/lidarbc/v1.1.0/schema.json (#26).

  • v1.0.0 is unchanged and stays published for the items that name it. This is the first version added under the never-edit rule.

crate 0.5.0 (2026-10-10)

crate now publishes JSON Schemas for the custom fields NGE’s STAC catalogues write, starting with lidarbc: (LidarBC’s objectstore paths and file names) and las: (the LAS format’s version and point format), at https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/stac/<prefix>/v1.0.0/schema.json (#23).

  • An item lists the URL in stac_extensions, and pystac then checks each field’s type: a point format of 11 or an unknown lidarbc: field fails validation.
  • A released version is never edited. A change is a new version beside it, and the site build fails if a version already on gh-pages would change or disappear. See the decision entry.

crate 0.4.0 (2026-09-02)

nge/track_sessions declares the four columns a crew fills in when they stop recording — track_name, track_type, track_description, named_by — and nge/track_annotations becomes the table of overrides for them.

  • The four are optional strings. An rfp-deployed tracking layer carries them (new upstream variant mergin-tracking-rfp-2026-08); a layer the plugin created on its own, or a GPX import, does not, and still conforms. A layer carrying some but not all is drift the reader must abort on — crate sees a frame, not a variant.
  • track_annotations now carries track_name, track_type and track_description, same names and types as the captured columns, and drops notes. The rule, stated once: a non-key annotation column sharing a captured column’s name overrides it where non-NA, coalesce(annotation, captured). A reader that assigns instead of coalescing blanks every unannotated session, which is why the rule is written down rather than left to each consumer.
  • track_type is an open string; the value list is the capture tool’s convention, recorded in the variant description and not enforced. See the decision entry for why captured beats annotated and why the annotation table was reshaped rather than extended.

crate 0.3.0 (2026-09-01)

nge/form_capture gains source_version, the upstream version a record was captured at.

  • Deliberately a column rather than a consumer-side manifest field, which is the opposite of the usual rule. That rule exists because stamping the upstream’s current version on every row churns a snapshot’s bytes for reasons unrelated to the data; a per-row capture version is fixed at capture and never moves. It is also what keeps (project, form, source_version, record_id) unique once a rebuild has restarted record_id at 1.
  • schema_version now documents how it is computed — <n>-<digest> over sorted name:type pairs of the capture’s own columns, hashing a joined string rather than a vector. Two producers computing it differently would give two genuinely different vintages the same version by accident, so the rule belongs with the declaration rather than with each caller.

crate 0.2.0 (2026-09-01)

New schema_only entry nge/form_capture: the envelope every captured field-form record carries — project, form, record_id, schema_version, captured_at — and nothing about what any observation means.

  • Vintage is a column, not a filename. Two shapes of one form are one logical table, distinguished by schema_version; a column absent from the older vintage is null there and schema_version says why, which is what separates “not asked” from “not answered”.
  • Per-form column meaning is still #13. The envelope leans on crt_schema_conform()’s documented floor-not-ceiling behaviour, so a form’s own columns pass through untouched until #13 defines them. See the decision entry for why an envelope rather than waiting, and why harvested_at is not a column.

crate 0.1.0 (2026-08-24)

crate can now declare a canonical shape for data it does not read, and can type a column as an instant.

  • crt_schema_conform() takes a data frame you already have and holds it to a registered canonical schema. crt_ingest() calls it rather than reimplementing validation and typing, so a file and a caller-supplied frame get identical treatment.
  • New canonical type datetime. It never moves an instant: a POSIXct has its timezone attribute stamped to UTC rather than converted, because several readers return correct UTC instants carrying no timezone label and “correcting” the rendering injects a real whole-hour error into every join.
  • The registry gains a kind column. schema_only entries declare a shape crate does not read; crt_ingest() aborts on them naming crt_schema_conform().
  • First schema_only entries: nge/track_sessions, nge/track_vertices and nge/track_annotations, the canonical shape of a GPS track. See the decision entry for why a track is two tables and why annotations are a third.
  • test-crt_registry_integrity.R walks the registry and the schemas directory rather than a hand-written list, so a row without a YAML, a YAML without a row, or a declared type nothing implements fails the suite.

crate 0.0.2 (2026-04-29)

Schema-as-contract scope settled and Convention C naming locked in (see crate#4).

  • Every function in the crate namespace now prefixed crt_*, family-namespaced (crt_schema_*, crt_registry_*, crt_handler_*).
  • New crt_schema_* family: crt_schema_read() (load YAML by relative path), crt_schema_apply() (canonical type enforcement), crt_schema_validate() (required-cols enforcement).
  • crt_ingest() now validates required cols and enforces canonical types after handler dispatch — schema YAML is the single source of truth.

crate 0.0.1 (2026-04-28)

Initial release. Source-explicit dispatcher (crt_ingest) plus first-instance handler for bcfp/user_habitat_classification (handles both pre-2026-04-26 long and current 2026-04-26 wide upstream variants → canonical wide).
